# openmetadata_api_collection (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata API collection. A collection groups the endpoints of one API service and carries their shared root URL.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_api_service" "payments" {
  name         = "payments-api"
  service_type = "Rest"
}

resource "openmetadata_api_collection" "pets" {
  name         = "pets"
  service      = openmetadata_api_service.payments.name
  endpoint_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"
  display_name = "Pets"
  description  = "Pet operations exposed by the payments API."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Collection name. Changing it replaces the collection, because the name is part of its fully qualified name.
- `service` (String) Fully qualified name of the parent API service. Changing it replaces the collection.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Markdown description of the collection.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.
- `endpoint_url` (String) Root URL shared by the endpoints in this collection.

### Read-Only

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name, in the form service.name.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `service_type` (String) OpenMetadata API service type, derived by the server from the parent service.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_api_collection.pets 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name, in the form service.collection.
terraform import openmetadata_api_collection.pets payments-api.pets
```
